addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

It adheres to the principles outlined in the [[RFC]: Hardware pluggable](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/11162), providing a hardware-pluggable interface that decouples the integration of the Ascend NPU with vLLM. 55 56 By using vLLM Ascend plugin, popular open-source models, including Transformer-like, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), Embedding, Multi-modal LLMs can run seamlessly on the Ascend NPU. 57 58 For detailed information on supported models and features, please refer to the [support matrix](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/user_guide/support_matrix/). 59 60 ## Prerequisites 61 62 - **main**: main branch, corresponds to the vLLM main branch, and is continuously monitored for quality through Ascend CI. 88 - **releases/vX.Y.Z**: development branch, created alongside new releases of vLLM. For example, `releases/v0.13.0` is the dev branch for vLLM `v0.13.0` version. 89 90 Below are the maintained branches: 91 92 | Branch | Status | Note | 93 |------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------| 94 | main | Maintained | CI commitment for vLLM main branch and vLLM v0.26.0 tag | 95 | releases/v0.13.0 | Maintained | Only bug fixes are allowed, and no new release tags anymore. | 96 | releases/v0.18.0 | Maintained | CI commitment for vLLM 0.18.0 version | 97 | releases/v0.23.0 | Maintained | CI commitment for vLLM 0.23.0 version | 98 | rfc/ | Maintained | [Feature branches](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/community/versioning_policy.html#feature-branches) for collaboration | 99 100 Please refer to [Versioning policy](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/community/versioning_policy.html) for more details. 101 102 ## Contributing 103 104 See [CONTRIBUTING](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/developer_guide/contribution/index.html) for more details, which is a step-by-step guide to help you set up the development environment, build and test. 105 106 We welcome and value any contributions and collaborations: 107 108 - Please let us know if you encounter a bug by [filing an issue](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues) 109 - Please use [User forum](https://discuss.vllm.ai/c/hardware-support/vllm-ascend-support) for usage questions and help. 110 111 ## Weekly Meeting 112 113 - vLLM Ascend Weekly Meeting: 114 - Wednesday, 15:00 - 16:00 (UTC+8, [Convert to your timezone](https://dateful.com/convert/gmt8?t=15)) 115 116 ## License 117 118 Apache License 2.0, as found in the [LICENSE](./LICENSE) file. 119

1	# vLLM Ascend Development Guidelines
2	
3	This document provides instructions for contributors to the vLLM Ascend project. Please read and follow these guidelines to ensure code quality, maintainability, and consistency.
4	
5	---
6	
7	## Table of Contents
8	
9	- [Setup and Environment](#setup-and-environment)
10	    - [Environment Variables](#environment-variables)
11	    - [Environment Variable Review Requirement](#environment-variable-review-requirement)
12	- [Testing](#testing)
13	    - [Unit and System Tests](#unit-and-system-tests)
14	    - [Running Tests](#running-tests)
15	- [Code Style](#code-style)
16	    - [Python Conventions](#python-conventions)
17	    - [Naming Conventions](#naming-conventions)
18	- [NPU-Specific Considerations](#npu-specific-considerations)
19	    - [Tensor item() Operations](#tensor-item-operations)
20	    - [Memory and Performance](#memory-and-performance)
21	- [Model and Plugin Architecture](#model-and-plugin-architecture)
22	    - [vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture](#vllm-ascend-plugin-architecture)
23	    - [Patching Requirement](#patching-requirement)
24	    - [Model Runner Changes](#model-runner-changes)
25	- [Commit Messages and Pull Requests](#commit-messages-and-pull-requests)
26	    - [Commit Message Format](#commit-message-format)
27	- [Review Checklist](#review-checklist)
28	    - [Code Quality](#code-quality)
29	    - [Testing](#testing-1)
30	    - [Documentation](#documentation)
31	    - [NPU Considerations](#npu-considerations)
32	    - [Commit and PR](#commit-and-pr)
33	- [Quick Start for Contributors](#quick-start-for-contributors)
34	- [References](#references)
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Setup and Environment
39	
40	### Environment Variables
41	
42	All environment variables must be defined in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` using the centralized `env_variables` dictionary.
43	
44	**Requirements:**
45	
46	- Add documentation for each environment variable in the `env_variables` dict comment
47	- Specify default values and valid ranges
48	- Indicate whether the variable is sensitive (credentials, keys)
49	
50	**Example:**
51	
52	```python
53	import os
54	
55	env_variables = {
56	    "VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ": lambda: int(os.getenv("VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ", 1)),
57	    # ...
58	}
59	```
60	
61	**Never**: Hardcode environment variable names throughout the codebase. Reference them from the central module using `from vllm_ascend import envs`.
62	
63	### Environment Variable Review Requirement
64	
65	**Strict Review Required**: All new environment variables must undergo code review.
66	
67	Reviewers must verify:
68	
69	- The variable name follows the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention
70	- Default value is appropriate for all supported hardware
71	- Documentation is added to the `env_variables` dict
72	- The variable is used in a performance-critical path
73	
74	---
75	
76	## Testing
77	
78	### Unit and System Tests
79	
80	**Requirement**: All new functionality requires corresponding tests.
81	
82	- **Unit Tests (UT)**: Located in `tests/ut/`, cover core logic, edge cases, and error conditions
83	- **System Tests (ST)**: Located in `tests/e2e/`, verify end-to-end behavior and integration points
84	- **Nightly Tests**: Include benchmarks for NPU-specific code paths in `tests/e2e/nightly/`
85	
86	**Test Coverage Guidelines:**
87	
88	- New features: Tests must cover happy path and failure modes
89	- Bug fixes: Tests must include a regression test for the bug
90	- Performance-critical code: Include benchmarks and performance regression tests
91	
92	### Running Tests
93	
94	```bash
95	
96	
97	# Run specific unit test file
98	pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py
99	
100	# Run specific unit test
101	pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py::test_prepare_inputs
102	
103	# Run NPU-specific tests (requires NPU hardware)
104	pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/aclgraph/test_aclgraph_accuracy.py::test_default_full_and_piecewise_res_consistency
105	```
106	
107	**Requirement**: Run all tests locally before requesting review. Verify tests pass on NPU hardware for NPU-specific changes.
108	
109	---
110	
111	## Code Style
112	
113	### Python Conventions
114	
115	- **Imports**: All imports at the top of the file. Valid exceptions:
116	    - Circular imports (use inline imports)
117	    - Lazy loading for worker/isolation processes
118	    - Type-checking imports wrapped in `if TYPE_CHECKING:`
119	
120	- **Global Variables**: Avoid new global variables. Pass dependencies explicitly through function parameters.
121	
122	    **Allowed:**
123	    - Constants named `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` in `envs.py`)
124	    - Immutable configuration objects
125	
126	    **Requires Approval:**
127	    - Any new mutable global state
128	
129	- **No Magic Numbers**: Use named constants with descriptive names:
130	
131	    ```python
132	    # Bad
133	    if seq_len > 2048: ...
134	
135	    # Good
136	    MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH = 2048
137	    if seq_len > MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH: ...
138	    ```
139	
140	- **Descriptive Naming**: Use names that describe functionality, not implementation details.
141	
142	    ```python
143	    # Bad
144	    is_deepseek_v3_r1
145	    flag1
146	    tmp_var
147	
148	    # Good
149	    supports_dynamic_temperature
150	    uses_speculative_decoding
151	    ```
152	
153	### Naming Conventions
154	
155	- **Classes**: `PascalCase` (e.g., `NPUModelRunner`, `AscendSampler`, `ACLGraphManager`)
156	- **Functions/Methods**: `snake_case` (e.g., `forward_pass`, `compute_attention`)
157	- **Constants**: `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ`)
158	- **Variables**: `snake_case` (e.g., `token_ids`, `sequence_lengths`)
159	
160	---
161	
162	## NPU-Specific Considerations
163	
164	### Tensor item() Operations
165	
166	**Warning**: `tensor.item()` operations cause synchronization overhead on NPU when the `tensor` is on device.
167	
168	If the `tensor` is a device tensor, calling `item()` will triggers a synchronous data transfer from NPU to CPU. This can severely degrade performance in hot paths, causing `AsyncScheduler` to block here.
169	
170	**Review Requirements:**
171	
172	1. Profile performance impact before merging
173	2. Consider alternative patterns:
174	    - Keep values on device when possible
175	    - Batch operations to reduce sync frequency
176	    - Use device-side operations (e.g., `torch.argmax`, `torch.sum`)
177	3. Document when `item()` is unavoidable (e.g., logging, conditional logic)
178	
179	**Example Patterns:**
180	
181	```python
182	# Bad: In hot loop - causes sync per iteration
183	for tensor in tensors:
184	    value = tensor.item()
185	
186	# Better: Batch operations - single sync
187	values = [t.item() for t in tensors]  # Single batch sync
188	
189	# Good: Keep on device when possible
190	max_value = torch.max(tensor)  # No sync needed
191	if max_value > threshold:  # Comparison can stay on device
192	    ...
193	```
194	
195	### Memory and Performance
196	
197	Additional NPU-specific best practices:
198	
199	- Avoid CPU-NPU memory transfers in hot paths
200	- Prefer in-place operations where safe (e.g., `x.add_()`, `x.mul_()`)
201	- Monitor memory fragmentation, especially for long-running processes
202	- Test with realistic workloads on actual NPU hardware (Ascend 910B/C)
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Model and Plugin Architecture
207	
208	### vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture
209	
210	vLLM Ascend is a **hardware plugin** that integrates with upstream vLLM via the pluggable hardware interface. It does not add new model files directly.
211	
212	**Required Pattern**: Model-specific functionality should be implemented via:
213	
214	1. **Patching** (in `vllm_ascend/patch/`):
215	    - `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/` - Platform-level patches (distributed, scheduling)
216	    - `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` - Worker-level patches (model-specific behavior)
217	    - Example: `patch_deepseek.py` modifies upstream Deepseek model behavior
218	    - Patch is not the best solution for all cases. Use it when necessary.
219	
220	2. **Inheritance**:
221	    - `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)` - Extend vLLM model runner with NPU-specific behavior
222	    - `AscendSampler` - Extend vLLM sampler with NPU-specific operations
223	    - Add NPU-specific components via composition (e.g., `AclGraphManager`)
224	    - Custom Operators - NPU-specific custom operators (e.g., `AscendRMSNorm`)
225	
226	3. **External upstream contributions** where appropriate
227	
228	### Patching Requirement
229	
230	**Strict Review Required**: All new patches must undergo thorough architectural review.
231	
232	Reviewers must verify:
233	
234	- The patch targets the correct upstream component
235	- The patch is minimal and focused
236	- Performance implications are understood
237	- A long-term plan exists for upstream contribution
238	
239	**Example Patch Pattern:**
240	
241	```python
242	# vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_deepseek.py
243	from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2 import DeepseekV2Model
244	
245	def forward(self, input_ids, positions, ...):
246	    # NPU-specific forward implementation
247	    ...
248	
249	DeepseekV2Model.forward = forward  # Patch upstream class
250	```
251	
252	### Model Runner Changes
253	
254	**Strict Review Required**: All new behaviors added to `model_runner` must undergo thorough architectural review.
255	
256	Reviewers must verify:
257	
258	- The necessity of the new behavior (why can't this be in a patch?)
259	- Performance implications on NPU hardware
260	- Compatibility with existing model implementations
261	- Long-term maintainability and test coverage
262	
263	**NPU Model Runner Files:**
264	
265	- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py` - vLLM v1 model runner
266	- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` - vLLM v2 model runner
267	- `vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py` - Ascend 310P model runner
268	
269	---
270	
271	## Commit Messages and Pull Requests
272	
273	### Commit Message Format
274	
275	Follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format and **must include a sign-off**:
276	
277	```bash
278	git commit -s -m "<type>: <summary>" -m "<body - explaining what changed and why>"
279	```
280	
281	Or using the full message format:
282	
283	```txt
284	<type>: <summary>
285	
286	<body - explaining what changed and why>
287	
288	Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
289	```
290	
291	**Valid Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`
292	
293	**Good Examples:**
294	
295	```txt
296	feat(npu): add flash attention support for Ascend CANN
297	
298	- Implements FlashAttention-2 kernel for NPU backend
299	- Reduces memory usage by 30% compared to baseline
300	
301	fix(model_runner): correct padding token handling
302	
303	- Fixes token padding that caused incorrect attention masks
304	- Addresses issue #1234
305	
306	perf: avoid CPU-NPU sync in attention computation
307	
308	- Inline computation to avoid tensor.item() calls
309	- Improves throughput by 15%
310	```
311	
312	**Bad Examples:**
313	
314	```txt
315	fix bug
316	add feature
317	update code
318	```
319	
320	### Pull Request Title Format
321	
322	PR titles should follow the format: `[Type][Module] Description`
323	
324	- **Type**: The type of change (e.g., `CI`, `Doc`, `BugFix`, `Feat`, `Platform`, `Refactor`)
325	- **Module**: The affected module (optional, e.g., `Misc`, `Model`, `Worker`)
326	- **Description**: Brief description of the change
327	
328	**Examples:**
329	
330	- `[Doc][Misc] Update contribution guidelines`
331	- `[BugFix] Fix CPU binding logic`
332	- `[CI] Update image build workflow`
333	
334	### Pull Request Template
335	
336	When creating a PR, please follow the template in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and ensure the following sections are completed:
337	
338	> **Note**: The PR description will be automatically updated by GitHub Actions to include vLLM version info at the bottom. If you update the PR description via API or CLI, make sure to preserve the `- vLLM version:` and `- vLLM main:` lines.
339	
340	- **What this PR does / why we need it?** - Clearly describe the changes and their purpose
341	- **Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?** - Indicate if there are any user-visible changes
342	- **How was this patch tested?** - Describe how you tested the changes. Examples:
343	    - Unit tests added/updated: list the test files
344	    - Manual testing: provide the test steps and commands
345	    - CI testing: indicate if only CI verification is needed
346	
347	---
348	
349	## Review Checklist
350	
351	Before merging, verify:
352	
353	### Code Quality
354	
355	- [ ] Code follows style guidelines (naming, imports, no magic numbers)
356	- [ ] No global state added without justification
357	- [ ] Patching pattern used correctly (if applicable)
358	- [ ] No direct model file additions
359	
360	### Testing
361	
362	- [ ] New tests added for new functionality (`tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`)
363	- [ ] Existing tests pass
364	- [ ] NPU-specific tests verified on actual hardware
365	- [ ] Performance benchmarks included where applicable
366	
367	### Documentation
368	
369	- [ ] Environment variables documented
370	- [ ] Public APIs documented
371	- [ ] User-facing changes reflected in docs
372	
373	### NPU Considerations
374	
375	- [ ] `tensor.item()` usage reviewed for performance impact
376	- [ ] No unnecessary CPU-NPU transfers in hot paths
377	- [ ] Memory usage verified on NPU hardware
378	
379	### Commit and PR
380	
381	- [ ] Commit messages are clear and descriptive, following Conventional Commits format
382	- [ ] **All commits are signed off** (`git commit -s`)
383	- [ ] PR is created from your fork repository, not directly from the main repository
384	- [ ] PR description is complete, following the PR template
385	- [ ] All review comments addressed
386	
387	---
388	
389	## Quick Start for Contributors
390	
391	1. Install development dependencies: `pip install -e .[dev]`
392	2. Run tests: `pytest tests/`
393	3. Check linting: `ruff check vllm_ascend/`
394	4. Format code: `ruff format vllm_ascend/`
395	5. Make your changes following guidelines in this document
396	6. Add tests for new behavior
397	7. Run full test suite before committing
398	8. Commit with sign-off: `git commit -s`
399	9. Run linting check before pushing:
400	   ```bash
401	   bash format.sh ci
402	   ```
403	   > **Note**: This check is required for **all file types**, including markdown files. If `markdownlint` modifies files, re-add them with `git add` and commit again.
404	10. Push to your fork repository (NOT the main repository):
405	
406	   ```bash
407	   git remote add myfork https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/vllm-ascend.git
408	   git push -u myfork your-branch-name
409	   ```
410	
411	11. Create a PR from your fork to the main repository with clear description
412	
413	---
414	
415	## References
416	
417	- [vLLM Hardware Plugin RFC](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/11162)
418	- [Documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/)
419	- [Contributors Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/community/contributors.html)
420

# vLLM Ascend Development Guidelines

This document provides instructions for contributors to the vLLM Ascend project. Please read and follow these guidelines to ensure code quality, maintainability, and consistency.

---

## Table of Contents

- [Setup and Environment](#setup-and-environment)
    - [Environment Variables](#environment-variables)
    - [Environment Variable Review Requirement](#environment-variable-review-requirement)
- [Testing](#testing)
    - [Unit and System Tests](#unit-and-system-tests)
    - [Running Tests](#running-tests)
- [Code Style](#code-style)
    - [Python Conventions](#python-conventions)
    - [Naming Conventions](#naming-conventions)
- [NPU-Specific Considerations](#npu-specific-considerations)
    - [Tensor item() Operations](#tensor-item-operations)
    - [Memory and Performance](#memory-and-performance)
- [Model and Plugin Architecture](#model-and-plugin-architecture)
    - [vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture](#vllm-ascend-plugin-architecture)
    - [Patching Requirement](#patching-requirement)
    - [Model Runner Changes](#model-runner-changes)
- [Commit Messages and Pull Requests](#commit-messages-and-pull-requests)
    - [Commit Message Format](#commit-message-format)
- [Review Checklist](#review-checklist)
    - [Code Quality](#code-quality)
    - [Testing](#testing-1)
    - [Documentation](#documentation)
    - [NPU Considerations](#npu-considerations)
    - [Commit and PR](#commit-and-pr)
- [Quick Start for Contributors](#quick-start-for-contributors)
- [References](#references)

---

## Setup and Environment

### Environment Variables

All environment variables must be defined in `vllm_ascend/envs.py` using the centralized `env_variables` dictionary.

**Requirements:**

- Add documentation for each environment variable in the `env_variables` dict comment
- Specify default values and valid ranges
- Indicate whether the variable is sensitive (credentials, keys)

**Example:**

```python
import os

env_variables = {
    "VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ": lambda: int(os.getenv("VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ", 1)),
    # ...
}
```

**Never**: Hardcode environment variable names throughout the codebase. Reference them from the central module using `from vllm_ascend import envs`.

### Environment Variable Review Requirement

**Strict Review Required**: All new environment variables must undergo code review.

Reviewers must verify:

- The variable name follows the `VLLM_ASCEND_*` naming convention
- Default value is appropriate for all supported hardware
- Documentation is added to the `env_variables` dict
- The variable is used in a performance-critical path

---

## Testing

### Unit and System Tests

**Requirement**: All new functionality requires corresponding tests.

- **Unit Tests (UT)**: Located in `tests/ut/`, cover core logic, edge cases, and error conditions
- **System Tests (ST)**: Located in `tests/e2e/`, verify end-to-end behavior and integration points
- **Nightly Tests**: Include benchmarks for NPU-specific code paths in `tests/e2e/nightly/`

**Test Coverage Guidelines:**

- New features: Tests must cover happy path and failure modes
- Bug fixes: Tests must include a regression test for the bug
- Performance-critical code: Include benchmarks and performance regression tests

### Running Tests

```bash


# Run specific unit test file
pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py

# Run specific unit test
pytest -sv tests/ut/ops/test_prepare_finalize.py::test_prepare_inputs

# Run NPU-specific tests (requires NPU hardware)
pytest -sv tests/e2e/pull_request/one_card/aclgraph/test_aclgraph_accuracy.py::test_default_full_and_piecewise_res_consistency
```

**Requirement**: Run all tests locally before requesting review. Verify tests pass on NPU hardware for NPU-specific changes.

---

## Code Style

### Python Conventions

- **Imports**: All imports at the top of the file. Valid exceptions:
    - Circular imports (use inline imports)
    - Lazy loading for worker/isolation processes
    - Type-checking imports wrapped in `if TYPE_CHECKING:`

- **Global Variables**: Avoid new global variables. Pass dependencies explicitly through function parameters.

    **Allowed:**
    - Constants named `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE` in `envs.py`)
    - Immutable configuration objects

    **Requires Approval:**
    - Any new mutable global state

- **No Magic Numbers**: Use named constants with descriptive names:

    ```python
    # Bad
    if seq_len > 2048: ...

    # Good
    MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH = 2048
    if seq_len > MAX_CONTEXT_LENGTH: ...
    ```

- **Descriptive Naming**: Use names that describe functionality, not implementation details.

    ```python
    # Bad
    is_deepseek_v3_r1
    flag1
    tmp_var

    # Good
    supports_dynamic_temperature
    uses_speculative_decoding
    ```

### Naming Conventions

- **Classes**: `PascalCase` (e.g., `NPUModelRunner`, `AscendSampler`, `ACLGraphManager`)
- **Functions/Methods**: `snake_case` (e.g., `forward_pass`, `compute_attention`)
- **Constants**: `ALL_UPPER_CASE` (e.g., `MAX_BATCH_SIZE`, `VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_NZ`)
- **Variables**: `snake_case` (e.g., `token_ids`, `sequence_lengths`)

---

## NPU-Specific Considerations

### Tensor item() Operations

**Warning**: `tensor.item()` operations cause synchronization overhead on NPU when the `tensor` is on device.

If the `tensor` is a device tensor, calling `item()` will triggers a synchronous data transfer from NPU to CPU. This can severely degrade performance in hot paths, causing `AsyncScheduler` to block here.

**Review Requirements:**

1. Profile performance impact before merging
2. Consider alternative patterns:
    - Keep values on device when possible
    - Batch operations to reduce sync frequency
    - Use device-side operations (e.g., `torch.argmax`, `torch.sum`)
3. Document when `item()` is unavoidable (e.g., logging, conditional logic)

**Example Patterns:**

```python
# Bad: In hot loop - causes sync per iteration
for tensor in tensors:
    value = tensor.item()

# Better: Batch operations - single sync
values = [t.item() for t in tensors]  # Single batch sync

# Good: Keep on device when possible
max_value = torch.max(tensor)  # No sync needed
if max_value > threshold:  # Comparison can stay on device
    ...
```

### Memory and Performance

Additional NPU-specific best practices:

- Avoid CPU-NPU memory transfers in hot paths
- Prefer in-place operations where safe (e.g., `x.add_()`, `x.mul_()`)
- Monitor memory fragmentation, especially for long-running processes
- Test with realistic workloads on actual NPU hardware (Ascend 910B/C)

---

## Model and Plugin Architecture

### vLLM Ascend Plugin Architecture

vLLM Ascend is a **hardware plugin** that integrates with upstream vLLM via the pluggable hardware interface. It does not add new model files directly.

**Required Pattern**: Model-specific functionality should be implemented via:

1. **Patching** (in `vllm_ascend/patch/`):
    - `vllm_ascend/patch/platform/` - Platform-level patches (distributed, scheduling)
    - `vllm_ascend/patch/worker/` - Worker-level patches (model-specific behavior)
    - Example: `patch_deepseek.py` modifies upstream Deepseek model behavior
    - Patch is not the best solution for all cases. Use it when necessary.

2. **Inheritance**:
    - `NPUModelRunner(GPUModelRunner)` - Extend vLLM model runner with NPU-specific behavior
    - `AscendSampler` - Extend vLLM sampler with NPU-specific operations
    - Add NPU-specific components via composition (e.g., `AclGraphManager`)
    - Custom Operators - NPU-specific custom operators (e.g., `AscendRMSNorm`)

3. **External upstream contributions** where appropriate

### Patching Requirement

**Strict Review Required**: All new patches must undergo thorough architectural review.

Reviewers must verify:

- The patch targets the correct upstream component
- The patch is minimal and focused
- Performance implications are understood
- A long-term plan exists for upstream contribution

**Example Patch Pattern:**

```python
# vllm_ascend/patch/worker/patch_deepseek.py
from vllm.model_executor.models.deepseek_v2 import DeepseekV2Model

def forward(self, input_ids, positions, ...):
    # NPU-specific forward implementation
    ...

DeepseekV2Model.forward = forward  # Patch upstream class
```

### Model Runner Changes

**Strict Review Required**: All new behaviors added to `model_runner` must undergo thorough architectural review.

Reviewers must verify:

- The necessity of the new behavior (why can't this be in a patch?)
- Performance implications on NPU hardware
- Compatibility with existing model implementations
- Long-term maintainability and test coverage

**NPU Model Runner Files:**

- `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py` - vLLM v1 model runner
- `vllm_ascend/worker/v2/model_runner.py` - vLLM v2 model runner
- `vllm_ascend/_310p/model_runner_310p.py` - Ascend 310P model runner

---

## Commit Messages and Pull Requests

### Commit Message Format

Follow the [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format and **must include a sign-off**:

```bash
git commit -s -m "<type>: <summary>" -m "<body - explaining what changed and why>"
```

Or using the full message format:

```txt
<type>: <summary>

<body - explaining what changed and why>

Signed-off-by: Your Name <your.email@example.com>
```

**Valid Types**: `feat`, `fix`, `perf`, `refactor`, `test`, `docs`, `chore`

**Good Examples:**

```txt
feat(npu): add flash attention support for Ascend CANN

- Implements FlashAttention-2 kernel for NPU backend
- Reduces memory usage by 30% compared to baseline

fix(model_runner): correct padding token handling

- Fixes token padding that caused incorrect attention masks
- Addresses issue #1234

perf: avoid CPU-NPU sync in attention computation

- Inline computation to avoid tensor.item() calls
- Improves throughput by 15%
```

**Bad Examples:**

```txt
fix bug
add feature
update code
```

### Pull Request Title Format

PR titles should follow the format: `[Type][Module] Description`

- **Type**: The type of change (e.g., `CI`, `Doc`, `BugFix`, `Feat`, `Platform`, `Refactor`)
- **Module**: The affected module (optional, e.g., `Misc`, `Model`, `Worker`)
- **Description**: Brief description of the change

**Examples:**

- `[Doc][Misc] Update contribution guidelines`
- `[BugFix] Fix CPU binding logic`
- `[CI] Update image build workflow`

### Pull Request Template

When creating a PR, please follow the template in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` and ensure the following sections are completed:

> **Note**: The PR description will be automatically updated by GitHub Actions to include vLLM version info at the bottom. If you update the PR description via API or CLI, make sure to preserve the `- vLLM version:` and `- vLLM main:` lines.

- **What this PR does / why we need it?** - Clearly describe the changes and their purpose
- **Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?** - Indicate if there are any user-visible changes
- **How was this patch tested?** - Describe how you tested the changes. Examples:
    - Unit tests added/updated: list the test files
    - Manual testing: provide the test steps and commands
    - CI testing: indicate if only CI verification is needed

---

## Review Checklist

Before merging, verify:

### Code Quality

- [ ] Code follows style guidelines (naming, imports, no magic numbers)
- [ ] No global state added without justification
- [ ] Patching pattern used correctly (if applicable)
- [ ] No direct model file additions

### Testing

- [ ] New tests added for new functionality (`tests/ut/` or `tests/e2e/`)
- [ ] Existing tests pass
- [ ] NPU-specific tests verified on actual hardware
- [ ] Performance benchmarks included where applicable

### Documentation

- [ ] Environment variables documented
- [ ] Public APIs documented
- [ ] User-facing changes reflected in docs

### NPU Considerations

- [ ] `tensor.item()` usage reviewed for performance impact
- [ ] No unnecessary CPU-NPU transfers in hot paths
- [ ] Memory usage verified on NPU hardware

### Commit and PR

- [ ] Commit messages are clear and descriptive, following Conventional Commits format
- [ ] **All commits are signed off** (`git commit -s`)
- [ ] PR is created from your fork repository, not directly from the main repository
- [ ] PR description is complete, following the PR template
- [ ] All review comments addressed

---

## Quick Start for Contributors

1. Install development dependencies: `pip install -e .[dev]`
2. Run tests: `pytest tests/`
3. Check linting: `ruff check vllm_ascend/`
4. Format code: `ruff format vllm_ascend/`
5. Make your changes following guidelines in this document
6. Add tests for new behavior
7. Run full test suite before committing
8. Commit with sign-off: `git commit -s`
9. Run linting check before pushing:
   ```bash
   bash format.sh ci
   ```
   > **Note**: This check is required for **all file types**, including markdown files. If `markdownlint` modifies files, re-add them with `git add` and commit again.
10. Push to your fork repository (NOT the main repository):

   ```bash
   git remote add myfork https://github.com/YOUR_USERNAME/vllm-ascend.git
   git push -u myfork your-branch-name
   ```

11. Create a PR from your fork to the main repository with clear description

---

import importlib.util
import os
import sys

_triton_available = importlib.util.find_spec("triton") is not None

# main2main compatibility: stub triton.experimental.gluon modules that
# vllm main requires but triton-ascend 3.2.1 does not provide. Runs at
# module-import time, which is triggered by vllm.platforms plugin
# discovery (importing vllm_ascend to resolve the plugin's `register()`
# callback) before any `from triton.experimental import gluon` import
# - including subprocesses such as `python -m vllm.model_executor.models.registry`.
if os.getenv("VLLM_VERSION", "") != "0.26.0":
    from types import ModuleType

    for _gluon_stub in (
        "triton.experimental.gluon",
        "triton.experimental.gluon.language",
    ):
        if _gluon_stub not in sys.modules:
            sys.modules[_gluon_stub] = ModuleType(_gluon_stub)

    # main2main compat: `_aggregate` was added to triton.language.core in
    # vllm main post-0.26.0. Stub it here so vllm.triton_utils can import it
    # without breaking on triton-ascend 3.2.1. Skip if triton is not
    # installed at all (e.g. 310P or CPU-UT environments).
    if _triton_available:
        try:
            import triton.language.core as _tl_core  # type: ignore[import-untyped]
        except Exception:
            pass
        else:
            if not hasattr(_tl_core, "_aggregate"):
                _tl_core._aggregate = lambda *a, **kw: None

_GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED = False


def _ensure_global_patch():
    """Apply process-wide vLLM patches before engine-core initialization.

    vLLM loads general plugins in engine-core subprocesses. E2E test
    conftest hooks do not run there, so global patches that affect scheduler
    and engine code must also be applied through these plugin entry points.
    """
    global _GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED
    if _GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED:
        return

    from vllm_ascend.utils import adapt_patch

    adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)
    _GLOBAL_PATCH_APPLIED = True


def register():
    """Register the NPU platform."""

    return "vllm_ascend.platform.NPUPlatform"


def register_connector():
    _ensure_global_patch()

    from vllm_ascend.distributed.kv_transfer import register_connector
    from vllm_ascend.distributed.weight_transfer import register_engine

    register_connector()
    register_engine()


def register_model_loader():
    _ensure_global_patch()

    from .model_loader.netloader import register_netloader
    from .model_loader.rfork import register_rforkloader

    register_netloader()
    register_rforkloader()


def register_service_profiling():
    _ensure_global_patch()

    from .profiling_config import generate_service_profiling_config

    generate_service_profiling_config()


def register_model():
    from vllm_ascend.patch.hunyuan_vl_processor_compat import (
        install_hunyuan_vl_processor_compat,
    )

    from .models import register_model

    install_hunyuan_vl_processor_compat()

    register_model()

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import os
from importlib import import_module, util
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any
from uuid import uuid4

import torch
import vllm.envs as envs_vllm
from vllm.logger import logger
from vllm.platforms import Platform, PlatformEnum

# todo: please remove it when solve cuda hard code in vllm
os.environ["VLLM_DISABLE_SHARED_EXPERTS_STREAM"] = "1"

from vllm.v1.attention.backends.registry import AttentionBackendEnum

from vllm_ascend.ascend_config import init_ascend_config

# isort: off
from vllm_ascend.utils import (
    ASCEND_QUANTIZATION_METHOD,
    COMPILATION_PASS_KEY,
    COMPRESSED_TENSORS_METHOD,
    FP8_METHOD,
    AscendDeviceType,
    bootstrap_custom_op_env,
    check_kv_extra_config,
    enable_sfa_dcp_replicated_indexer,
    get_ascend_device_type,
    is_moe_model,
    model_uses_sfa_sparse,
    refresh_block_size,
    update_cudagraph_capture_sizes,
    is_310p,
    enable_sp,
)

# Since vllm-project/vllm#43746, DeepSeek V4 model classes no longer
# carry @support_torch_compile. This makes vLLM auto-enable the breakable
# cudagraph PIECEWISE path, which is not supported on Ascend yet.
envs_vllm.VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH = False
logger.info(
    "Breakable cudagraph is force disabled on Ascend because DeepSeek V4 PIECEWISE cudagraph is not supported yet."
)

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from vllm.config import ModelConfig, VllmConfig
    from vllm.utils import FlexibleArgumentParser
else:
    ModelConfig = None
    VllmConfig = None
    FlexibleArgumentParser = None

_CUSTOM_OP_REGISTERED = False
# Delete after the driver is released; temporarily hard-coded to 4
MAX_CAPTURE_SIZES_FOR_950 = 4


def config_deprecated_logging():
    """Configure deprecated logging format, when used deprecated codes
    in vllm-ascend.
    """
    import logging
    import warnings

    # Customize warning format to be one line
    def one_line_formatwarning(message, category, filename, lineno, line=None):
        return f"{filename}:{lineno}: {category.__name__}: {message}"

    warnings.formatwarning = one_line_formatwarning

    logging.captureWarnings(True)
    warnings.simplefilter("once", DeprecationWarning)

    vllm_logger = logging.getLogger("vllm")
    warnings_logger = logging.getLogger("py.warnings")

    # Propagate vllm logger handlers to warnings logger, to keep the same
    # format with vllm
    if vllm_logger.handlers:
        warnings_logger.handlers = []

        for handler in vllm_logger.handlers:
            warnings_logger.addHandler(handler)

    warnings_logger.propagate = False


def prune_capture_sizes_for_950(vllm_config):
    original_sizes = vllm_config.compilation_config.cudagraph_capture_sizes
    if not original_sizes:
        return
    if len(original_sizes) <= MAX_CAPTURE_SIZES_FOR_950:
        return
    step = (len(original_sizes) - 1) / (MAX_CAPTURE_SIZES_FOR_950 - 1)
    indices = [round(i * step) for i in range(MAX_CAPTURE_SIZES_FOR_950)]
    indices[0], indices[-1] = 0, len(original_sizes) - 1
    sampled_sizes = [original_sizes[i] for i in indices]
    update_cudagraph_capture_sizes(vllm_config, sampled_sizes)
    logger.warning(
        "Adjusted ACL graph batch sizes for model: %d → %d sizes due to HDK incompatibility"
        "and this warning will be cleared soon.",
        len(original_sizes),
        MAX_CAPTURE_SIZES_FOR_950,
    )


class NPUPlatform(Platform):
    _enum = PlatformEnum.OOT
    device_name: str = "npu"
    device_type: str = "npu"

class AscendConfig:

    """

    def __init__(self, vllm_config: "VllmConfig"):
        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
        additional_config = vllm_config.additional_config if vllm_config.additional_config is not None else {}
        self._check_mooncake_c8_kv_cache_quant(vllm_config)

        xlite_graph_config = additional_config.get("xlite_graph_config", {})
        self.xlite_graph_config = XliteGraphConfig(xlite_graph_config, vllm_config)

        ascend_compilation_config = additional_config.get("ascend_compilation_config", {})
        self.ascend_compilation_config = AscendCompilationConfig(**ascend_compilation_config)

        ascend_fusion_config = additional_config.get("ascend_fusion_config", {})
        self.ascend_fusion_config = AscendFusionConfig(**ascend_fusion_config)

        finegrained_tp_config = additional_config.get("finegrained_tp_config", {})
        self.finegrained_tp_config = FinegrainedTPConfig(finegrained_tp_config, vllm_config)

        eplb_config = additional_config.get("eplb_config", {})
        self.eplb_config = EplbConfig(eplb_config)

        from vllm_ascend import envs as ascend_envs

        self.scheduler_config = SchedulerConfig(
            additional_config,
            balance_env_value=ascend_envs.VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING,
        )
        if self.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.enabled:
            max_batched = vllm_config.scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens
            if max_batched < self.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.min_chunk:
                logger.warning(
                    "max_num_batched_tokens is smaller than profiling_chunk_config.min_chunk. "
                    "max_num_batched_tokens=%d, min_chunk=%d. "
                    "Clamping min_chunk to %d to avoid it being silently ignored.",
                    max_batched,
                    self.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.min_chunk,
                    max_batched,
                )
                self.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.min_chunk = max_batched
        if (
            self.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.enabled
            and vllm_config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size <= 1
        ):
            raise ValueError(
                "profiling_chunk_config requires pipeline parallelism (pp > 1). "
                "Please set --pipeline-parallel-size to a value greater than 1, "
                "or disable profiling_chunk_config."
            )

        self.enable_flashcomm1 = self._get_config_value(
            additional_config,
            "enable_flashcomm1",
            "VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1",
            ascend_envs.VLLM_ASCEND_ENABLE_FLASHCOMM1,
        )
        if self.scheduler_config.profiling_chunk_config.enabled and self.scheduler_config.enable_balance_scheduling:
            raise ValueError(
                "profiling_chunk_config and balance scheduling (enable_balance_scheduling) "
                "cannot be enabled at the same time. Please disable one of them."
            )

        # Dump / PrecisionDebugger configuration
        self.dump_config_path = self._resolve_dump_config_path(additional_config)

        # Log configuration
        self.ascend_log_path = additional_config.get(
            "ascend_log_path",
            os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), "ascend", "log", "vllm_ascend"),
        )

        self.enable_shared_expert_dp = (
            additional_config.get("enable_shared_expert_dp", False)
            and vllm_config.parallel_config.enable_expert_parallel
            and vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size > 1
        )
        from vllm_ascend.utils import enable_sp

# isort: skip_file
import os

os.environ["VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE"] = "True"
os.environ["VLLM_WORKER_MULTIPROC_METHOD"] = "spawn"

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams


def main():
    prompts = [
        "Hello, my name is",
        "The president of the United States is",
        "The capital of France is",
        "The future of AI is",
    ]

    # Create a sampling params object.
    sampling_params = SamplingParams(max_tokens=100, temperature=0.0)
    # Create an LLM.
    # NOTE: To access output.metrics (e.g., first_token_time, finished_time),
    # set disable_log_stats=False. By default, vLLM disables log stats and
    # output.metrics will be None. See issue #5027 for details.
    llm = LLM(model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")

    # Generate texts from the prompts.
    outputs = llm.generate(prompts, sampling_params)
    for output in outputs:
        prompt = output.prompt
        generated_text = output.outputs[0].text
        print(f"Prompt: {prompt!r}, Generated text: {generated_text!r}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    notify_kv_cache_written,
    split_decodes_and_prefills,
    update_paged_attention_graph_param,
    using_paged_attention,
)
from vllm_ascend.compilation.acl_graph import (
    get_draft_graph_params,
    get_draft_graph_prefill_params,
    get_graph_params,

from vllm_ascend.utils import is_950, weak_ref_tensors

# default max value of sliding window size
SWA_INT_MAX = 2147483647
_ATTN_KEYS_BUFFER = None


@register_backend(AttentionBackendEnum.CUSTOM, "ASCEND")
class AscendAttentionBackend(AttentionBackend):
    accept_output_buffer: bool = True

    @staticmethod
    def get_name() -> str:
        # HACK(Ronald1995): vllm `initialize_kv_cache` method in model runner v2 make
        # attention name assertion, we just set name to FLASH_ATTN to avoid assertion error.
        # rectify this when vllm disable the assertion.
        return "CUSTOM" if not envs_vllm.VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER else "FLASH_ATTN"

    @staticmethod
    def get_impl_cls() -> type["AscendAttentionBackendImpl"]:
        if enable_dcp():
            from vllm_ascend.attention.context_parallel.attention_cp import AscendAttentionDCPImpl

            return AscendAttentionDCPImpl
        return AscendAttentionBackendImpl

17	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
18	# This module manage the patch for vllm. There are two folders in this module:
19	# - platform: contains the patches applied before worker starts. It's called by
20	#             `vllm_ascend.utils.adapt_patch(is_global_patch=True)` in
21	#             `vllm_ascend.platform.NPUPlatform.pre_register_and_update()` function.
22	# - worker: contains the patches applied when worker starts. It's called by
23	#           `vllm_ascend.utils.adapt_patch(is_global_patch=False)` in
24	#           each worker's `__init__` function.
25	#
26	# Once a new patch is added in vllm-ascend, please add the patch description into this file as well.
27	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	
29	# What's Patched and how it works:
30	# --------------------------------
31	# * Platform Patch:
32	# =================
33	# Entries are listed in alphabetical order by file name.
34	#
35	# ** 1. File: platform/patch_balance_schedule.py**
36	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
37	#   1. `vllm.v1.engine.core.EngineCoreProc.run_engine_core`
38	#      `vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler.Scheduler`
39	#    Why:
40	#       vLLM v1 scheduling currently enables chunkedprefill by default, which processes prefill and decode
41	#       requests simultaneously in a single scheduling session. This can impact the overall system throughput
42	#       and performance in some scenarios.
43	#    How：
44	#       Set --additional-config '{"enable_balance_scheduling": true}' or
45	#       set environmental variable VLLM_ASCEND_BALANCE_SCHEDULING=1 (deprecated).
46	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
47	#       https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/29721
48	#    Future Plan:
49	#       Remove this patch when vLLM merge the PR.
50	#
51	# ** 3. File: platform/patch_distributed.py**
52	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
53	#   1. `torch.distributed.all_reduce`, `torch.distributed.broadcast`
54	#    Why:
55	#       tensor alignment for 310p
56	#    How：
57	#       rewrite all_reduce and broadcast in torch.distributed
58	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
59	#       No, not ready yet.
60	#    Future Plan:
61	#       Find a better way to support tensor alignment for 310p without this patch.
62	#
63	# ** 4. File: platform/patch_dp_device_ids.py**
64	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
65	#   1. `vllm.v1.core.dp_utils.get_physical_gpu_ids_for_local_dp_rank`
66	#    Why:
67	#       PR #45026 removed the per-process device isolation that older vLLM
68	#       versions performed internally. Application-level DP (e.g.
69	#       `offline_data_parallel.py`) now has to slice ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES
70	#       per rank itself, but the upstream helper still expects the env var to
71	#       contain ALL devices for ALL ranks and tries to read it with the
72	#       `local_dp_rank * world_size` offset. With a sharded env var, that
73	#       offset is out of range and the helper raises IndexError (wrapped in the
74	#       user-facing "Error computing device indices for ..." message).
75	#    How：
76	#       Patch `get_physical_gpu_ids_for_local_dp_rank` so it tolerates a
77	#       pre-sharded ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES env var (one slice per DP rank),
78	#       instead of unconditionally applying `local_dp_rank * world_size` as an
79	#       offset into it.
80	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
81	#       https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45026
82	#    Future Plan:
83	#       Remove this patch once upstream `get_physical_gpu_ids_for_local_dp_rank`
84	#       handles a pre-sharded visible-devices env var, or vLLM-Ascend stops
85	#       relying on application-level device slicing for DP.
86	#
87	# ** 5. File: platform/patch_fused_moe.py**
88	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
89	#   1. `vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.FusedMoE`
90	#    Why:
91	#       vllm's FusedMoE is a factory function (not a class). deepseek_v2 and
92	#       other models do `from vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe import FusedMoE`
93	#       and call it directly, so on Ascend we must redirect it to AscendMoERunner
94	#       before any model is imported.
95	#    How：
96	#       Patch the FusedMoE binding in both the package `__init__` and the layer
97	#       module so model imports pick up the Ascend runner. `worker/patch_fused_moe.py`
98	#       reuses this platform patch to avoid double-wrapping the factory during
99	#       worker initialization.
100	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
101	#       No, vllm-ascend-specific MoE runner integration.
102	#    Future Plan:
103	#       Remove this patch once upstream exposes a backend dispatch / plugin hook
104	#       for selecting the MoE runner implementation.
105	#
106	# ** 6. File: platform/patch_kv_cache_coordinator.py**
107	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
108	#   1. `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_coordinator.HybridKVCacheCoordinator.find_longest_cache_hit_per_group`
109	#    Why:
110	#       In PD disaggregation with hybrid Mamba models, the D side receives
111	#       FullAttention KV blocks from the P side but has no local prefix-cache
112	#       hit for Mamba groups. Upstream's min-reduction across all KV groups
113	#       collapses the FullAttention hit length to 0, preventing partial
114	#       FullAttention-only prefix cache reuse on the D side.
115	#    How:
116	#       For Mamba hybrid models,
117	#       num_new_local_computed_tokens should be the FA hit
118	#       length. This value is passed to the connector's
119	#       get_num_new_matched_tokens which computes:
120	#       external = total - local_computed.
121	#       Using the FA hit skips re-transferring FA blocks
122	#       already cached on D-side.
123	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
124	#       https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42524
125	#       https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44243
126	#    Future Plan:
127	#       Remove this patch when vLLM PR #42524 and #44243 is included in the supported
128	#       upstream vLLM version.
129	#
130	# ** 7. File: platform/patch_kv_cache_utils.py**
131	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
132	#   1. `vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils.resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`
133	#      `vllm.v1.engine.core.resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes`
134	#    Why:
135	#       vLLM PR #40860 added a restriction that hybrid KV cache groups with
136	#       multiple block sizes do not support decode context parallelism.
137	#       This restriction is correct for CUDA but not for Ascend, which

1012	# ** 22. File: worker/patch_routed_experts_capture.py**
1013	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1014	#   1. `vllm.model_executor.layers.fused_moe.routed_experts_capturer.RoutedExpertsCapturer.capture`
1015	#    Why:
1016	#       The upstream implementation doesn't support vllm-ascend specific MoE communication types
1017	#       (ALLTOALL and MC2). In the SP + modular-kernel path, the original code cannot correctly
1018	#       handle tensor splitting and all-gather operations on NPU, especially when tokens are
1019	#       unevenly distributed across TP ranks or padded to max_tokens in MC2 mode.
1020	#    How：
1021	#       Override the capture method to add support for vllm-ascend's MoECommType:
1022	#         - Check `_EXTRA_CTX.moe_comm_type` to determine if ALLTOALL or MC2 mode is active
1023	#         - Calculate correct gather_topk_ids_shape based on communication type:
1024	#           * ALLTOALL: uses actual token_num_per_dp for shape calculation
1025	#           * MC2: uses padded max_tokens * tp_size for shape calculation
1026	#         - Properly handle tensor_split and all_gather operations for NPU distributed communication
1027	#    Future Plan:
1028	#       Remove this patch when upstream vLLM supports MoE communication type abstraction that
1029	#       can be extended by hardware plugins like vllm-ascend.
1030	#
1031	# ** 23. File: worker/patch_step3p5.py**
1032	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1033	#   1. `vllm.model_executor.models.step3p5.Step3p5Attention.forward`
1034	#    Why:
1035	#       Add split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope support for step3.5/3.7. This model can't use
1036	#       fusion pass to enable this op because of 2 reasons: 1) Step uses
1037	#       Gemmanorm instead of normal norm, so existing fusion pass can't be
1038	#       matched. 2) Step has 2 kinds of attention layer (full attention and
1039	#       sliding window attention), each has different number of q_head. Right
1040	#       now, torch.compile will use same pattern to match different attention
1041	#       layer so there will be shape mismatch in split op.
1042	#    How:
1043	#       Monkey-patch Step3p5Attention.forward to enable split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.
1044	#    Future Plan:
1045	#       Remove this patch once torch.compile fully supports matching pattern from
1046	#       op's params.
1047	#
1048	# ** 24. File: worker/patch_triton.py**
1049	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1050	#   1. `vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.ops`, `vllm.model_executor.layers.fla.ops`,
1051	#      `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.gumbel.gumbel_sample`
1052	#    Why:
1053	#       triton ops in vLLM perform not good on NPU. And there is no dispatch mechanism for triton ops.
1054	#    How：
1055	#       override triton ops in vLLM with ascend implementation
1056	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1057	#       Let vLLM support triton ops dispatch.
1058	#    Future Plan:
1059	#       Remove this patch when vLLM support the dispatch function.
1060	#
1061	#   2. `triton.next_power_of_2`
1062	#    Why:
1063	#       The Triton version bundled with torch_npu on Ascend NPU
1064	#       does not include `next_power_of_2`, which is called by
1065	#       upstream vLLM and vLLM-Ascend code in 94+ places.
1066	#       Additionally, when Triton is not available (HAS_TRITON=False),
1067	#       vLLM uses TritonPlaceholder which also lacks this function.
1068	#    How：
1069	#       Import `triton` from vllm.triton_utils (which handles both
1070	#       real Triton and TritonPlaceholder) and inject `next_power_of_2`
1071	#       onto the module, reusing `vllm.utils.math_utils.next_power_of_2`.
1072	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1073	#       No, torch_npu Triton compatibility issue.
1074	#    Future Plan:
1075	#       Remove this patch when torch_npu's Triton includes
1076	#       next_power_of_2 or when vLLM no longer calls triton.next_power_of_2.
1077	#
1078	# ** 25. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_attn_utils.py**
1079	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1080	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.attn_utils.get_kv_cache_spec`
1081	#    Why:
1082	#       The current v2 worker still goes through the shared upstream v1 helper
1083	#       to build KV cache specs. For Ascend MLA layers that helper returns the
1084	#       generic `MLAAttentionSpec`, but NPU-side cache allocation and reshape
1085	#       logic expects `AscendMLAAttentionSpec`.
1086	#    How：
1087	#       Monkey-patch `get_kv_cache_spec` so regular attention layers keep the
1088	#       upstream behavior while MLA layers are rewritten to
1089	#       `AscendMLAAttentionSpec`, including the FA-quant head-size adjustment.
1090	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1091	#       No. This is a plugin-side compatibility patch for the current upstream
1092	#       helper path.
1093	#    Future Plan:
1094	#       Remove this patch once upstream adds a backend hook for KV cache spec
1095	#       construction or v2 worker no longer depends on the shared v1 helper.
1096	#
1097	# ** 26. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_block_table.py**
1098	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1099	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.block_table.BlockTables`
1100	#    Why:
1101	##      vllm-ascend need to initialize slot mapping as torch.int32 dtype,
1102	#       but vllm default is torch.int64 dtype.
1103	#    How：
1104	#       replace BlockTables with AscendBlockTables which initialize slot mapping
1105	#       as torch.int32 dtype.
1106	#    Future Plan:
1107	#       remove this patch when vLLM-ascend's BlockTables can initialize
1108	#       slot mapping as torch.int64 dtype.
1109	#
1110	# ** 27. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_dflash_speculator.py**
1111	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1112	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.dflash.speculator.DFlashCudaGraphManager`
1113	#    Why:
1114	#       The v2 DFlash spec-decode path uses upstream `DFlashCudaGraphManager`
1115	#       (CUDA graph) for spec decoding, which is not usable on Ascend.
1116	#    How：
1117	#       Replace `DFlashCudaGraphManager` with the Ascend `DFlashAclGraphManager`
1118	#       (ACL graph) on the upstream speculator module.
1119	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1120	#       No, vllm-ascend v2 spec-decode ACL graph integration.
1121	#    Future Plan:
1122	#       Remove this patch once upstream exposes a backend-dispatchable spec-decode
1123	#       graph manager abstraction.
1124	#
1125	# ** 28. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_eagle_speculator.py**
1126	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1127	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator.PrefillSpeculatorCudaGraphManager`,
1128	#      `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.spec_decode.autoregressive.speculator.DecodeSpeculatorCudaGraphManager`
1129	#    Why:
1130	#       The v2 Eagle spec-decode path uses upstream CUDA graph managers for
1131	#       prefill/decode spec decoding, which are not usable on Ascend.
1132	#    How：
1133	#       Replace the prefill/decode speculator graph managers on the upstream
1134	#       module with `PrefillEagleAclGraphManager` / `DecodeEagleAclGraphManager`
1135	#       (ACL graph).
1136	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1137	#       No, vllm-ascend v2 spec-decode ACL graph integration.
1138	#    Future Plan:
1139	#       Remove this patch once upstream exposes a backend-dispatchable spec-decode
1140	#       graph manager abstraction.
1141	#
1142	# ** 29. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_input_batch.py**
1143	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1144	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.input_batch.InputBatch`
1145	#    Why:
1146	#       vllm use InputBatch to make dummy tensors. in `model_runner.py` and `cudagraph_utils.py`
1147	#       which make it difficult to inherit from vllm methods.
1148	#    How：
1149	#       replace InputBatch with AscendInputBatch.
1150	#    Future Plan:
1151	#       remove this patch when vLLM-ascend's make_dummy behavior aligns with vLLM.
1152	#
1153	# ** 30. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_model_state.py**
1154	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1155	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.model_states.default.init_model_state`
1156	#    Why:
1157	##      vllm's prepare_attn in ModelState is different from vllm,
1158	#       we need to override init_model_state.
1159	#    How：
1160	#       Define AscendModelState and initialize it in init_model_state.
1161	#    Future Plan:
1162	#       remove this when vllm-ascend's attention metadata is align with vllm.
1163	#
1164	# ** 31. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_triton.py**
1165	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1166	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.logprob`, `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.penalties.apply_penalties`,
1167	#      `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.sample.gumbel.gumbel_sample`
1168	#    Why:
1169	#       triton ops in vLLM perform not good on NPU. And there is no dispatch mechanism for triton ops.
1170	#    How：
1171	#       override triton ops in vLLM with ascend implementation
1172	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1173	#       Let vLLM support triton ops dispatch.
1174	#    Future Plan:
1175	#       Remove this patch when vLLM support the dispatch function.
1176	#
1177	# ** 32. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py**
1178	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1179	#   1. `vllm.config.vllm.VllmConfig.use_v2_model_runner`
1180	#    Why:
1181	#       EngineCore subprocesses only load global/platform patches, while workers
1182	#       also import this compatibility module. The actual monkey-patch is defined
1183	#       in `platform/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py`.
1184	#    How：
1185	#       Reuse the platform patch so EngineCore and worker processes share the
1186	#       same `use_v2_model_runner` behavior.
1187	#    Related PR (if no, explain why):
1188	#       See platform/patch_use_v2_model_runner.py.
1189	#    Future Plan:
1190	#       Remove this module together with the platform patch once vllm-ascend
1191	#       fully supports the v2 model runner.
1192	#
1193	# ** 33. File: worker/patch_v2/patch_uva.py**
1194	# ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1195	#   1. `vllm.v1.worker.gpu.states.UvaBuffer`
1196	#    Why:
1197	#       ASCEND NPUs do not support UVA yet, so we need to wrap it in vLLM.
1198	#    How：

1200	#    Future Plan:
